subject: Conditional launch credits & monthly commit phasing — qualification
messages:
From: Emily Song <emily@skybound.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: monthly commit phasing + launch credits

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We ran an internal model and attached a first-pass monthly forecast for our upcoming product launch (SkyLaunch). Key ask: we expect a very high token volume for the first 6–10 weeks, then a drop to steady-state.

Questions:
- Do you support a step-up monthly commit where discounts increase as committed tokens ramp?
- Can Redwood offer conditional launch credits (one-time or temporary surge credits) for the initial high-traffic months while we ramp to committed levels?
- What contract cadence do you typically use for pilot -> full commit (monthly true-up vs fixed-step commits)?

We'd like a sketch of options for both commercial and operational guardrails (burst allowances, true-ups, caps). Procurement timeline is tight — we hope to finalize terms by end of month.

Attachment: Skybound_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Emily Song
Head of Platform Partnerships
Skybound AI
emily@skybound.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Song <emily@skybound.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: monthly commit phasing + launch credits

Hi Emily — thanks for the forecast, I reviewed the high-level numbers and looped in Marissa (AE) and Ben (pricing/finance). A few clarifying items so we can draft a concrete proposal: 

1) Can you confirm the aggressive-launch window months (you mentioned 6–10 weeks) — is that primarily Month 1–2 post-launch?
2) Do you expect most of the volume to be inference (per-token generation) or do you have a high embedding/semantic-search footprint as well?
3) Are there any regulatory/compliance constraints we should include (data residency, VPC/private deployment) or is hosted fine?

High-level options we often propose:
- Step-up commits: month-by-month committed tokens with defined discounts that escalate when hitting commit thresholds.
- Temporary launch credit: a capped credit pool applied to the first N tokens/month for M months if actual usage exceeds the committed baseline (helps buy down overage for launch spikes).
- Surge buffer: a short-lived elevated burst allowance for low-latency traffic with discounted overage true-up.

I'll have Marissa produce a term-sketch; Ben will double-check discount cadence against commit size. If you can share a short QPS/peak-per-minute number for the first 72 hours of launch that helps dimension surge capacity.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that accelerates. Proposed owners: Marissa for commercial, Ben for pricing, me for architecture.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue, North America
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Song <emily@skybound.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Rourke <liam@skybound.ai>, procurement@skybound.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: monthly commit phasing + launch credits

Hi Karthik / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick response. Answers below:

1) Aggressive window: primarily Month 1 and Month 2 (we project ~65% of first-quarter volume in the first 8 weeks), followed by a stepped decrease over Month 3–4 to steady-state by Month 5.
2) Mix: ~75% generation (per-token) and ~25% embeddings for retrieval.
3) Hosted is fine for this initial launch; we may revisit private deployment later. SOC2 is required prior to contract signature — we can handle any extra evidence requests.

Peak ask: during the first 72 hours we see burst peaks of ~1500 concurrent requests and sustained hourly token output that could be 3–4x steady-state. I attached an updated CSV with weekday/weekend seasonality profiles and a more granular month-by-month forecast.

Procurement timeline: desire to complete commercial terms by 10/29; legal will run a 7–10 day review.

Attachment: Skybound_Launch_Profile_v2.csv (csv)

Wanted to also flag that we are evaluating two models for pilot pricing: (A) a short pilot at consumption rates + option to convert to commit with retro credits; (B) a small-month fixed commit with a launch credit pool. Which approach tends to move faster from Redwood's side?

Thanks,
Emily
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Song <emily@skybound.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: monthly commit phasing + launch credits

Emily — appreciate the detail and the updated profile. Based on the forecast and peak numbers, here's a draft commercial structure we can take to procurement: 

1) Step-up monthly commit (recommended):
   - Months 1–2: Lower committed baseline with an elevated conditional launch credit applied to overage tokens up to a capped pool. That pool phases out at the end of Month 3.
   - Months 3–6: Commit steps up to a mid-level discount tier (X% off hosted per-token rates) when cumulative committed tokens hit defined thresholds.
   - Month 7+: Steady-state commit with standard committed discount tiers.

2) Temporary launch credit (mechanics):
   - Credit pool equivalent to Y% of projected Month 1 usage (applied to per-token invoicing as a one-time line item).
   - True-up at monthly cadence: actual usage reconciles against committed tokens; credits reduce overage charges during the launch window.

3) Surge buffer and latency SLAs:
   - We can enable a short-term elevated burst allowance (configurable) for the first 72 hours with a capped multiplier on committed throughput.
   - If you require firm latency SLOs for the burst window, we can attach an elevated SLA with an associated premium/credit tradeoff (we should scope with Priyom on the runtime side).

4) Pilot path options:
   - Option A (consumption->convert): fastest commercial cadence; sign an MSA + consumption terms, then convert with retroactive credits once commit is agreed. Legal turnaround tends to be quicker for this.
   - Option B (small fixed commit + credit): slightly slower but gives you committed pricing from Day 1 and cleaner true-up math.

Next steps I suggest: Marissa will circulate a short term-sheet with nominal discount bands and the proposed credit mechanics (attached). Ben will validate discount math and cap sizing. Priyom will connect with your eng team to validate peak configuration and burst controls. If that sounds good, can we target a 30-min call on 10/22 to lock the commercial path before your procurement push?

Attachment: Proposed_Term_Sheet.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Karthik
Head of Revenue, North America
Redwood Inference
